q: Logical behaviorism was modeled on Russell and Whitehead's treatment of numbers as:
w: States of the mathematician's brain
Eternal Platonic forms
Dispositions to count
e: Just as numbers were constructions out of sets, mental events were said to be logical constructions out of actual and possible behavior.

q: What does the logical behaviorist share with the dualist, per Putnam?
a: Brain events aren't part of what 'pain' means
w: Both believe in an immaterial Cartesian soul
Both hold that pain is just a brain state
Both reject all talk about behavior
e: What goes on in the brain has nothing to do with what we MEAN by 'pain'. Yet the behaviorist is as 'tough-minded' as the materialist in denying a Cartesian Mind-substance.

q: Putnam famously says of logical behaviorism: 'I come to ______ logical behaviorism, not to ______ it.'
w: Praise; bury
Defend; refute
Explain; criticize
e: He argues that even the weakened forms (analytic entailments, near-translation) are incorrect.

q: Putnam says 'pain' is a cluster-concept. What does he mean?
a: It's applied using several synthetic criteria
w: Pain is nothing but a cluster of behaviors
The word 'pain' has no meaning at all
Pain is defined by one necessary condition
e: Its application is controlled by a cluster of criteria, all of which are synthetic. The behaviorist would say 'pain stands for a cluster of phenomena'. That is NOT what Putnam means.

q: Putnam's disease analogy (polio, multiple sclerosis) is meant to show that:
a: Causes aren't logical constructions of effects
w: Diseases are really mental states in disguise
Pain is caused by a virus like polio
Symptoms define diseases by their meaning
e: Causes are not logical constructions out of their effects. 'Multiple sclerosis' means the disease normally responsible for certain symptoms, not the symptoms. Likewise pain normally causes pain behavior.

q: Putnam's conclusion about the relation of pains to responses is that pains:
w: Are identical to clusters of responses
Have no relation to responses at all
Are caused by clusters of responses
e: Are not clusters of responses, but (normally) the causes of clusters of responses. This is an empirical fact, and it doesn't rule out worlds where pains produce different responses or none.

a: Feel pain but hide the behavior
w: Feel no pain at all, ever
Exaggerate every little pain
Feel pain only in strong fields
e: Feel pain but suppress all involuntary pain behavior. They admit pain only in calm, well-modulated voices. It would be absurd to say they can't feel pain.

a: Suppress even verbal reports of pain
w: Have no brains inside their heads
Feel only pleasure and never pain
Communicate only by sending V-waves
e: Suppress even verbal reports of pain and pretend not to know the word. If pains were logical constructions out of behavior, X-worlders would behave so as not to have pains. But they do have them.

q: If the X-world story isn't self-contradictory, Putnam says this refutes even logical behaviorism's FIRST (weakest) thesis, which is:
a: Mind and behavior statements have analytic links
w: Mental talk can be translated exactly into behavior talk
Minds are nothing more than brains and their states
Behavior is the cause of pain and other sensations
e: There exist analytic entailments between mind-statements and behavior-statements. From 'X has a pain' by itself, no behavioral statement follows, not even one with 'normally' or 'probably'.

q: 'Last night at midnight everything doubled in length.' Putnam uses this 'pseudo-hypothesis' to argue that:
w: It is genuinely meaningless nonsense
Length turns out to be a mental property
It shows that behaviorism is correct
e: It actually has testable consequences (e.g., an apparent halving of the speed of light). It's the worst example of an untestable hypothesis. Things in philosophy are rarely as simple as they seem.

q: Why do 'V-waves' that decode into coherent English give better evidence than 'brain spikes'?
a: Coherent language can't arise by chance
w: V-waves are louder and easier to detect
Brain spikes don't actually exist at all
V-waves are a kind of outward behavior
e: Spikes could have almost any cause, but coherent language can't arise by chance. The 'null hypothesis' of chance can be dismissed, and coherence and simplicity then do real verifying work.

q: Putnam compares inferring X-worlders' pain via theory to inferring what from spectral lines in sunlight?
w: Water on Mars
Life on other planets
Gravity on the moon
e: We don't need to heat cadmium on the sun to verify it. Coherence with a vast body of theory is scientific verification.

q: The 'W-waves' (decoded as 'Ho, ho! are we fooling those Earthians!') show that:
a: Even brain-state principles can be given up
w: The X-worlders don't really exist at all
V-waves are a perfectly reliable signal
Logical behaviorism is true after all
e: Even the brain-state = pain principle could reasonably be given up, so it isn't a tautology. What's necessarily true is only: an organism in the same state as a human in pain in ALL relevant respects is in pain.

q: Putnam says the logical behaviorist's two escape moves ('change of meaning' and 'untestable') are, respectively:
a: Bad linguistics and bad scientific method
w: Sound logic and equally sound science
Dualism and materialism, respectively
Analytic truths and synthetic truths
e: Unreasonable linguistics and unreasonable scientific method. They're mutually supporting. 'The circle of reason is to be preferred to any of the many circles of unreason.'

q: In a footnote, Putnam sketches a fourth alternative (beyond dualism, materialism, behaviorism) in which states like pain are defined by:
w: Overt behavior
Physical-chemical makeup
Divine decree
e: Functional organization, which can be built into many possible physical constitutions. This is the seed of functionalism. 'Prefers A to B' doesn't tell us if a creature is carbon, silicon, or even disembodied.
